candidates.primary_query: ab welchem alter roller fahren vietnam
candidates.intent_rationale: Families travelling with teenagers and young backpackers want to know from what age someone may ride a moped or a motorbike in Vietnam, and what happens if a person under 18 rides a scooter of 50 cc or more.
candidates.content_angle: Explains Article 59(1) of Law 36/2024/QH15 (16 and over for mopeds, 18 and over for A1 and A licences) and the Decree 168/2024 Article 18 sanctions (a warning for riders aged 14 to 15, 400,000 to 600,000 VND for 16- and 17-year-olds on bikes of 50 cc or 4 kW and more), with what this means for families who rent scooters.
candidates.working_title: Ab welchem Alter darf man in Vietnam Roller fahren?

references.title: Consolidated text of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety (Law 36/2024/QH15), Government portal (Article 59 on age)
Government policy portal: full text of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP on road traffic administrative penalties (Article 18(1) and 18(4)(a))

distinct_from.reason: DE-S05 klärt, ob ein deutscher Führerschein in Vietnam gilt; dieses Thema behandelt die gesetzlichen Altersgrenzen für Mopeds und Motorräder unabhängig vom Führerschein.
DE-S02 vergleicht 50-cm³-Roller und Elektroroller als Mietfahrzeug; hier geht es darum, ab welchem Alter welches Fahrzeug gefahren werden darf und welche Sanktionen drohen.

candidates.intent_rationale: Expats and long-stay riders who hold or converted to a Vietnamese licence want to understand the 12-point licence system: how many points a violation costs, when points come back and what happens when all of them are gone.
candidates.content_angle: Explains Article 58 of Law 36/2024/QH15 (12 points, full restoration after 12 months without deductions, a traffic-law check after at least 6 months once all points are lost) and Articles 50 and 51 of Decree 168/2024 on how deductions and restorations are recorded and notified, with typical motorcycle deductions from Article 7(13) such as 2 points for riding on the sidewalk or carrying three people.
candidates.working_title: Punktesystem für den Führerschein in Vietnam: 12 Punkte und wie man sie verliert

references.title: Consolidated text of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety (Law 36/2024/QH15), Government portal (Article 58 on licence points)
Government policy portal: full text of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP (Articles 50 and 51 on deducting and restoring licence points, Article 7(13))

distinct_from.reason: DE-S38 erklärt das Umschreiben des deutschen Führerscheins in einen vietnamesischen; dieses Thema erklärt, wie das 12-Punkte-System danach funktioniert und wann Punkte verfallen oder zurückkommen.
DE-S14 beschreibt den Ablauf einer Polizeikontrolle am Straßenrand; hier geht es um die Punkte, die nach einem Bußgeldbescheid vom Führerschein abgezogen werden.

candidates.intent_rationale: Visitors riding in Hanoi meet traffic lights with countdown timers, arrow signals and flashing yellow and want to know exactly what each phase allows on a scooter, including whether they may turn while the main light is red.
candidates.content_angle: Explains Article 11(4) of Law 36/2024/QH15 (green, yellow, flashing yellow and red), the light types in QCVN 41:2024/BGTVT Article 6 (green arrows that alone permit a movement, a left arrow that also permits a U-turn unless prohibited, countdown timers, the red cross), and the Decree 168/2024 sanction of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 VND plus 4 points for ignoring traffic lights (Article 7(7)(c) and 7(13)(b)).
candidates.working_title: Ampeln in Vietnam: Was Gelb, Rot und Pfeile für Rollerfahrer bedeuten

Government policy portal: full text of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP (Article 7(7)(c) and 7(13)(b))

candidates.intent_rationale: Riders in Hanoi and on trips along the North-South railway cross many level crossings, some without barriers, and want to know when they must stop, how the warning signals work and what to do if the scooter stalls on the tracks.
candidates.content_angle: Explains Article 24 of Law 36/2024/QH15 (stop on the right before the stop line when a guard signals, red lights flash, a bell rings or the barrier moves; stop and look both ways at unguarded crossings; warn the train at once if a vehicle is stuck), the warning signs W.210 and W.211 and the alternating flashing red lights in QCVN 41:2024/BGTVT, and the bans on overtaking, U-turns and reversing at crossings.

candidates.primary_query: in der gruppe roller fahren vietnam
candidates.intent_rationale: Friends and tour groups who ride several rented scooters together want to know how to ride as a group legally and safely, because riding abreast, convoys and group speeding are specifically sanctioned in Vietnam.
candidates.content_angle: Explains the ban on riding abreast in Article 33(3)(a) of Law 36/2024/QH15 and the Decree 168/2024 Article 7 fines for three or more bikes abreast (600,000 to 800,000 VND), speeding in a group of two or more bikes and convoys that obstruct traffic (8,000,000 to 10,000,000 VND each, licence withdrawal for 10 to 12 months), plus practical advice on formation, spacing, signals and meeting points.
candidates.working_title: In der Gruppe Roller fahren in Vietnam: Regeln und Tipps für Touren

references.title: Consolidated text of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety (Law 36/2024/QH15), Government portal (Article 33(3))
Government policy portal: full text of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP (Article 7(3)(k), 7(9)(b), 7(9)(i) and 7(12)(b))

candidates.intent_rationale: Travellers who rented a scooter worry about traffic-camera fines that reach the rental shop after they have returned the bike, and want to know how such notices work, who is liable and how to avoid disputes over deductions from the deposit.
candidates.content_angle: Explains how violations recorded by cameras are handled under Decree 168/2024 Article 47: a notice to the registered owner by letter or the police traffic app, the owner's duty to help identify the rider, the rental contract and ID as evidence, and the consequences for a renter who does not respond; plus practical steps such as keeping the contract and agreeing at return how later notices are handled.

candidates.intent_rationale: Riders who received a traffic penalty decision in Vietnam want to know where and how to pay it, how long they have, what a late payment costs and how they get back documents the police kept until payment.
candidates.content_angle: Explains the payment channels (the National Public Service Portal dichvucong.gov.vn with a lookup by decision or record number and bank payment, or a transfer to the State Treasury account named in the decision), the time limit for executing a penalty decision, the 0.05 percent per day surcharge for late payment and how documents held by the police are returned by post or in person.

secondary_queries: roller mit dem fuß schieben vietnam
candidates.intent_rationale: When a rented scooter runs out of fuel or breaks down, travellers see locals tow it with a rope or push it with a foot from another bike and want to know whether that is legal and which safer alternatives exist.
candidates.content_angle: Explains that riders may not use a motorbike to tow or push another vehicle and passengers may not hold, pull or push other vehicles (Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 33(3)(đ) and 33(4)(c)), the Decree 168/2024 Article 7(3)(e) and (g) fines of 600,000 to 800,000 VND, and the alternatives: pushing the scooter on foot, calling the rental shop, roadside repairers and transport by truck.
candidates.working_title: Roller abschleppen oder mit dem Fuß schieben: Was in Vietnam erlaubt ist

candidates.intent_rationale: Visitors touring Vietnam by scooter in the hot season want to know how heat affects riding, how to recognise heat exhaustion and heatstroke, and how to plan rides, breaks, clothing and water.
candidates.content_angle: Uses the WHO heat and health fact sheet (avoid the hottest time of day, stay in the shade, perceived temperature in the sun 10 to 15 degrees higher, about one cup of water per hour and at least 2 to 3 litres a day, light loose clothing, heat raises accident risk, follow official heat warnings) to build a practical plan for scooter days in the Vietnamese summer.
